overview: Two types of DNA fragment ends produced by restriction enzyme digestion, differing in whether they leave overhanging single strands.
genZNote: Blunt ends: a clean, flat cut, no overhang. Sticky ends: a jagged cut leaving single-stranded overhangs that can grab a matching partner.

aspects.label: Overhang Present?
aspects.valueA: No overhang — both strands are cut at exactly the same position.
aspects.valueB: Yes — a short single-stranded overhang is left on each fragment.

aspects.label: Ease of Ligation
aspects.valueA: Harder to join efficiently, since there's no complementary overhang to guide pairing.
aspects.valueB: Easier and more efficient to join, since complementary overhangs base-pair before ligation.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Sticky ends are strongly preferred in genetic engineering because their complementary overhangs make ligating a gene into a vector far more efficient.
overlay.memoryTrick: Sticky ends 'stick' to their complementary partner before ligase seals them.
overlay.commonMisconception: Blunt-end cutting restriction enzymes are not 'worse' or obsolete — they're still useful when a specific palindromic sticky-end site isn't available in the sequence of interest.
